Surah al-Qital (Muhammad) [Madaniyya except verse 13, or Makkiyya; its verses are 38 or 39]

﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ from among the people of Makkah, ﴿and bar⁽¹⁾﴾ others ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., Islam, ﴿He has sent astray⁽²⁾﴾, i.e., He has nullified ﴿their deeds⁽³⁾﴾, such as feeding people food and maintaining ties of kinship. So they will find no reward for them in the Hereafter, but they will be recompensed for them in this world by His bounty, exalted is He.

Notes on terms:
(1) ṣaddū (صَدُّوا): from ṣadd, meaning to bar or turn away.
(2) aḍalla (أَضَلَّ): here meaning to render something void or lost, rather than to lead astray.
(3) a'mālahum (أَعْمالهمْ): "their deeds," i.e., their good works.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 2:

﴿And those who believe﴾, i.e., the Helpers (al-Ansar) and others, ﴿and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them﴾ He will forgive them ﴿their misdeeds and will amend their condition﴾ their state, so that they do not disobey Him.

﴿That﴾, i.e., the sending astray (nullifying) of their deeds and the expiation of their misdeeds, ﴿because﴾, owing to the fact that ﴿those who disbelieved followed falsehood﴾, namely Satan, ﴿and those who believed followed the truth﴾, namely the Qur'an, ﴿from their Lord.﴾ ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like that clarification, ﴿Allah sets forth for people their parables﴾, clarifying their states. That is, the disbeliever's deeds are nullified, and the believer is forgiven.

﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, then [strike] the striking of necks﴾: "ḍarb" (فَضَرْب) is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun) in the accusative, standing in place of the verb's own root (بَدَل مِن اللَّفْظ بِفِعْلِهِ), i.e., "then strike their necks," meaning "kill them." He expressed it as "striking of the necks" because killing most commonly occurs by striking the neck. ﴿Until when you have subdued them﴾: you have inflicted much killing upon them. ﴿Then bind firmly﴾: then hold back from them, take them captive, and bind firmly ﴿the bonds﴾: that with which captives are bound. ﴿Then either a favour afterwards﴾: a *maṣdar* standing in place of the verb's own root, i.e., you bestow favour upon them by releasing them without any compensation. ﴿Or ransom﴾: you ransom them for wealth or in exchange for Muslim captives. ﴿Until the war lays down its burdens﴾: i.e., its people. ﴿Its burdens﴾: its loads of weapons and other things, by the disbelievers embracing Islam or entering into a covenant. This is the limit (ghāyah) for both the killing and the taking of captives. ﴿That﴾: a predicate of an implied subject, i.e., the matter concerning them is what has been mentioned. ﴿And had God willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them﴾ without fighting. ﴿But﴾ He commanded you to it ﴿so that He may test some of you by means of others﴾: some of them in fighting, so that whoever among you is killed goes to Paradise, and whoever of them is killed goes to Hell. ﴿And those who were killed﴾: in another reading, "qātalū" (fought). The verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, when killing and wounds had spread among the Muslims. ﴿In the way of God, He will not let their deeds go astray﴾: "yuḍill" means "yuḥbiṭ," i.e., He will nullify them.

﴿He will guide them﴾ in this world and in the Hereafter to what benefits them, ﴿and will set their affairs right﴾, meaning their condition in both. As for what is in this world, it applies to those who were not killed, and they were included in "were killed" by way of *taghlib* (a rhetorical device in which one term of a pair is used to cover both).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 6:

﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.﴾ ʿarrafahā (made it known) means: bayyanahā (He clarified it) ﴿for them﴾, so that they find their way to their dwellings in it, and to their spouses and their servants, without needing to ask for directions (min ghayr istidlāl).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 7:

﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah﴾ i.e., His religion and His Messenger, ﴿He will support you﴾ against your enemy, ﴿and plant firmly your feet﴾ He will make you firm in the battlefield.

﴿And those who disbelieve﴾: these are the people of Makkah. It is the subject (mubtada', the topic of a nominal sentence), and its predicate (khabar, the comment that completes it) is "they shall stumble", which is indicated by what follows: ﴿so ruin for them﴾, meaning destruction and disappointment from Allah. ﴿And He will cause their deeds to go astray﴾ is conjoined (ʿutifa, joined by a conjunction) to "they shall stumble".

ذَلِكَ (That) refers to the ruin and misguidance (التَّعْس والإضْلال). بِأَنَّهُمْ كَرِهُوا ما أنْزَلَ اللَّه (because they disliked what Allah sent down) from the Qur'an, which contains the obligations (التَّكالِيف).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 10:

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ Allah destroyed them, [i.e., He destroyed] their selves, their children and their wealth. ﴿And for the disbelievers there are similar [outcomes]﴾, i.e., similar to the outcome of those before them.

This is the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 47, verse 11:

﴿That﴾ is the victory of the believers and the subjugation of the disbelievers, ﴿because Allah is the Protector﴾ (mawla), i.e., the Ally and Helper.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 47, verse 12:

﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believed and did righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. And those who disbelieved enjoy themselves [in this world] and eat as cattle eat.﴾ [In this world.] ﴿And the Fire is a residence for them.﴾ [I.e., that they are concerned only with their stomachs and their private parts, and do not turn their attention to the Hereafter.] ﴿And the Fire is a residence for them﴾ [a dwelling, a place of stay, and a final destination.]

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 13:

﴿And how many a town﴾, meaning how many, ﴿of towns﴾, meaning its people, ﴿which was mightier in power than your town﴾, Makkah, meaning its people, ﴿which expelled you﴾, the singular form of "town" is observed; ﴿We destroyed them﴾, the plural meaning of the first "town" is observed, ﴿and they had no helper﴾ against Our destruction.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 14:

﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence (bayyina) from his Lord﴾ — a proof and demonstration — and they are the believers, ﴿like one to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive﴾ — so he sees it as good — and they are the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿and who follow their own desires﴾ — in the worship of idols; meaning, there is no equivalence between the two.

Translation of the passage from Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 47 (Muhammad), verse 15:

﴿A parable of﴾, i.e., the description of ﴿the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised﴾, the common feature among its inhabitants. It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿therein are rivers of water unchanging﴾ — "āsin is read with the long vowel (al-madd) and the short vowel (al-qasr), like ḍārib and ḥadhir — i.e., not changing, unlike the water of this world, which changes through some external cause; ﴿and rivers of milk whose taste does not change﴾, unlike the milk of this world, since it comes out of the udders; ﴿and rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾, unlike the wine of this world, which is repulsive when drunk; ﴿and rivers of clarified honey﴾, unlike the honey of this world, which, because it comes out of the bellies of bees, mixes with wax and other things. ﴿And for them therein﴾ are kinds ﴿of every fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord﴾ — He is pleased with them, along with His bounty to them through what has been mentioned, unlike the master of slaves in this world, who may, despite his kindness to them, be displeased with them. ﴿Is it like one who abides in the Fire﴾ — the predicate of an implied subject, i.e., "Is he who is in this bliss [like one who abides in the Fire]?" ﴿and they are given to drink boiling water﴾, i.e., extremely hot, ﴿which cuts their bowels﴾, i.e., their intestines, so that they come out from their posteriors. It is the plural of mi'an (ma'a), with the short vowel, and its alif is from a yā', as in their saying mīʿān.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 16:

﴿And among them﴾ i.e., among the disbelievers, ﴿are those who listen to you﴾ during the Friday sermon, and they are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun). ﴿Until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge﴾ i.e., to the learned among the Companions, among them Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, mockingly and derisively, ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾ The word "ma'dha" is read with both the madd (long vowel) and the qasr (short vowel); it means "just now," i.e., a moment ago, meaning: we will not return to him. ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ with disbelief, ﴿and they followed their desires﴾ in hypocrisy.
ﷻ "And those who are guided" — they are the believers — "He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety" — He inspires them with that by which they guard against the Fire.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 47, verse 18:

﴿Are they waiting﴾ (فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ) for what they await, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿except the Hour﴾ (إلّا السّاعَة) ﴿that it come upon them﴾ (أنْ تَأْتِيهِمْ), a substitution of inclusion (بَدَل اشْتِمال) from "the Hour", meaning: the matter is nothing but that it come upon them ﴿suddenly﴾ (بَغْتَة), i.e., unexpectedly (فَجْأَة). ﴿Its signs have already come﴾ (فَقَدْ جاءَ أشْراطها), i.e., its indicators (عَلاماتها), among them the sending of the Prophet (ﷺ), the splitting of the moon, and the smoke. ﴿So how will they have their reminder when the Hour comes to them?﴾ (فَأَنّى لَهُمْ إذا جاءَتْهُمْ ذِكْراهُمْ), i.e., it will not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 19:

﴿So know that there is no god but Allah﴾, i.e., persist, O Muhammad, in your knowledge of that, which is beneficial on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, on its account. It was said to him this, despite his infallibility, so that his community might follow his example, and he did so. He ﷺ said: "Indeed I ask Allah for forgiveness a hundred times every day." ﴿And for the believing men and the believing women﴾: in this there is an honouring of them, by the command to their Prophet to ask forgiveness for them. ﴿And Allah knows your movement﴾, your going about, [i.e., your] occupation during the day, ﴿and your resting place﴾, your abode, [i.e., your] place of lodging to your sleeping places at night. That is, He is aware of all your conditions, none of which is hidden from Him, so beware of Him. The address is to the believers and others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 20:

﴿And those who believe say﴾, seeking jihad, ﴿"Why has a surah not been sent down?"﴾ (i.e., "Why has it not been sent down?"), ﴿a surah in which fighting is mentioned.﴾ ﴿But when a clear surah is sent down﴾, meaning, none of it has been abrogated, ﴿and fighting is mentioned in it﴾, meaning, its call to it, ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning doubt, and they are the hypocrites, ﴿looking at you with the look of one who has fainted from death﴾, out of fear of it and aversion to it; meaning, they fear fighting and dislike it. ﴿So woe to them﴾: "awla" is a mubtada' (subject) whose predicate is

﴿Obedience and honorable speech﴾, i.e., good for you. ﴿And when the matter is resolved upon﴾, i.e., fighting is made obligatory. ﴿Then if they had been truthful to Allah﴾ in faith and obedience. The clause beginning with ﴿if﴾ (law) is the response (jawab, the apodosis of the conditional clause) to ﴿when﴾ (idha).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 47, verse 22:

﴿Then, would you perhaps﴾ (fa-hal 'asaytum; the sīn may be read with kasra or with fatḥa, and there is an iltifat (shift of grammatical person) here from the third person, the absent (ghayba), to the second person, the addressed (khiṭāb)), meaning: perhaps you, ﴿if you turn away﴾, i.e., turn away from faith, ﴿will cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship﴾, i.e., you will return to the matters of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) of tyranny (baghy) and fighting.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 23:

﴿Those﴾, i.e., the corrupters, ﴿whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf﴾ to hearing the truth, ﴿and blinded their eyes﴾ to the path of guidance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 24:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ so that they would recognize the truth. ﴿Or﴾ rather, ﴿upon hearts﴾ that they have, ﴿locks upon them﴾, so they do not comprehend it.

﴿Indeed, those who turned back﴾ into hypocrisy (*nifaq*, hypocrisy) ﴿on their heels after guidance had become clear to them, Satan made it seem fair to them﴾, meaning he adorned it for them, ﴿and granted them respite﴾. The verb *wa-umlī* is read with a *ḍamma* on its first letter (*umlī*) and with a *fatḥa* (*amlā*), and with the *lām*. The one who grants respite is Satan, by God's will, exalted is He, so He is the one who misguides them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 47, verse 26:

﴿That﴾ i.e., their being led astray, ﴿is because they said to those who hated what Allah has revealed﴾ i.e., to the polytheists, ﴿"We will obey you in part of the matter"﴾ i.e., in aiding them against the Prophet ﷺ and discouraging the people from fighting jihad alongside him. They said this secretly, but Allah Most High exposed it. ﴿But Allah knows their secrets﴾ — with the hamzah pronounced with a fatḥah (asrārahum, "their secrets"), the plural of sirr (secret); and with it pronounced with a kasrah (isrārahum), it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) meaning "their secret-keeping" or "their concealing."

﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ [i.e., how will] their state be ﴿إذْ تَوَفَّتْهُمْ المَلائِكَة يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ [when the angels take their souls, striking], ﴾ ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ is a ḥāl (a grammatical circumstantial qualifier describing the state of the subject at the time of the action) of the angels ﴿وُجُوههمْ وأَدْبارهمْ﴾ [their faces and their backs], i.e., their backs, ﴿بِمَقامِع مِن حَدِيد﴾ [with maqāmi' (iron maces) of iron].
﴿That﴾: the death (tawaffi) in the state mentioned, ﴿because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure﴾, that is, acting in what pleases Him.
﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring forth their rancor?﴾ He will reveal their malice toward the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 30:

﴿And had We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks.﴾ "We would have made them known to you" (ʿarrafnākahum). The lām is repeated in ﴿so you would surely recognize them by their mark (sīmāhum)﴾, where "mark" (simā) means their sign. And ﴿you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech (laḥn al-qawl)﴾: the wāw is for an omitted oath, and what follows it is the answer to that oath. "Laḥn al-qawl" means its meaning, i.e. when they speak in your presence, by alluding to what disparages the affairs of the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 31:

﴿And We will surely test you﴾ We will examine you with jihad and other things, ﴿until We make evident﴾ knowledge of manifestation, ﴿those of you who strive [in the way of Allah] and are steadfast﴾ in jihad and other things, ﴿and We will test﴾ We will make manifest ﴿your affairs﴾ regarding your obedience and disobedience in jihad and other things, with the ya' and the nun in the three verbs.

Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah, [the way of truth], and oppose the Messenger, [i.e., they contend with him], after guidance has become clear to them, [which is the meaning of the way of Allah], will never harm Allah in the least, and He will nullify their deeds, [i.e., render them void], such as charity and the like, so that they will have no reward for them in the Hereafter. It was revealed concerning those among the Companions of Badr who fed (the polytheists), or concerning Qurayza and al-Nadir.
O you who believe, obey God and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds ﴿by acts of disobedience,﴾ for example.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 34:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah﴾ — His path, which is guidance — ﴿and then die while they are disbelievers, Allah will never forgive them﴾. It was revealed concerning the people of the well (aṣḥāb al-qalīb).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 35:

﴿So do not weaken﴾ (tahinu), i.e. do not become feeble, ﴿and call to peace﴾ (as-salm), with the sin pronounced with a fatha or a kasra, i.e. reconciliation with the disbelievers, when you meet them, ﴿while you are the superior ones﴾ (al-a'lawn). The waw of the root of the verb has been elided from it: al-aghlabun, i.e. the victorious, the dominant. ﴿And Allah is with you﴾ with help and victory, ﴿and He will not deprive you of﴾ (yatirakum), i.e. He will not diminish for you, ﴿your deeds﴾, i.e. their reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 36:

﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement.﴾ That is, occupation with it (al-ishtighal fihā) is play and amusement. ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah﴾ and that belongs to the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿He will give you your rewards and will not ask of you your wealth﴾ all of it, but rather the obligatory zakat (al-zakāh al-mafrūdah) from it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 47, verse 37:

﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring forth your rancor.﴾ He presses in demanding it. ﴿You would be stingy, and He would bring forth your rancor﴾ — the stinginess — ﴿against the religion of Islam.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 47, verse 38:

﴿Here you are﴾ O ﴿you who are called to spend in the way of God﴾ (what has not been enjoined upon you). ﴿Among you are some who are stingy﴾, and whoever is stingy, he is only stingy against his own self. It is said: "bakhila 'alayhi" and "bakhila 'anhu" (both are used, with 'ala and 'an). ﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient﴾ (free of your spending), ﴿and you are the needy﴾ (towards Him). ﴿And if you turn away﴾ (from His obedience), ﴿He will replace you with another people﴾, i.e., He will make them your substitute, ﴿then they will not be like you﴾ in turning away from His obedience, but rather they will be obedient to Him, mighty and majestic is He.
